title: One-at-a-time sensitivity analysis of two bias layers reports robustness that the joint analysis does not support
question: Do one-at-a-time sensitivity analyses of population transportability and component invariance bound their joint effect on a cross-gap contrast, or can the layers offset and report spurious robustness?
design: Population-level calculation on a logistic model: omitted-modifier imbalance, component main-effect drift and component-by-modifier drift varied one at a time and jointly over elicited ranges at three scales, with independent and dependent elicitations.
answer: No. With an omitted modifier (population layer) and component drift (bridge layer) acting on one cross-gap log odds ratio of -0.20, each one-at-a-time curve stayed within 0.16 and never reversed the decision, while the joint elicited box reached a bias of -0.41 and 7% of it reversed the decision; 23% to 26% of the box lay outside the one-at-a-time envelope at every scale. Component-by-modifier drift, which current tooling excludes, moved the estimate by 0.04 alone because it acts through its product with the modifier imbalance.
findings: Scale 1: one-at-a-time envelope -0.156 to 0.157; joint -0.413 to 0.341; 7% of the box reverses the decision.
Masking: in 4% of the box both layers exceed 0.1 in absolute value and the net bias is below 0.05.
Elicited dependence: 32% to 34% of draws outside the one-at-a-time envelope when the layers are positively correlated, 21% to 24% independent, 5% to 12% negatively correlated.
not_answered: Population-level calculation on one logistic model; no sampling, component network fit or survival scale; joint covariate law known, so the cost of eliciting it is not measured; component non-additivity and backbone interactions not included. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Bias of the reported target marginal log odds ratio of the cross-gap contrast
methods_compared: joint sensitivity region over both layers
n_sim: Population-level calculation: 21^3 grid and 4000 elicited draws x 3 dependence structures at 3 scales
